title: From No Notables to No Influentials
statement: Let $\Psi$ be a finite family of predicates on signs, let $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $0<\alpha<\beta\le1$, and let $e:[0,1]\to[0,1]$ tend to $0$ as its argument tends to $0$ through positive values. Suppose a family of randomized testers, one for each positive cube dimension, uses only predicates in $\Psi$, accepts every coordinate dictator with probability at least $\beta$, and accepts every function whose stable influences at parameter $1-\varepsilon$ are all at most $\varepsilon$ with probability at most $\alpha+e(\varepsilon)$ for each $\varepsilon\in[0,1]$. Then the same testers use only predicates in $\Psi$, accept every dictator with probability at least $\beta$, and accept every function whose influences at parameter $1$ are all at most $\varepsilon$ with probability at most $\alpha+e(\varepsilon)$ for each $\varepsilon\in[0,1]$.
hypotheses_covered: Every tester check uses a predicate in $\Psi$
Every dictator is accepted with probability at least $\beta$
For each $\varepsilon\in[0,1]$, functions whose stable influences at parameter $1-\varepsilon$ are all at most $\varepsilon$ are accepted with probability at most $\alpha+e(\varepsilon)$
